sources.entry: Dozzle | Realtime log viewer for docker containers

summary.one_liner: Dozzle is a lightweight, web-based real-time viewer for Docker container logs that stores no log files.
summary.what_it_does: Dozzle runs as a small container that mounts the Docker socket and serves a web UI for watching container logs live. It offers fuzzy search over container names, regex search of logs, and SQL-style queries over logs. Users can split the screen to view several logs at once and see live memory and CPU stats per container. It supports multi-user authentication, including forward proxy authorization, plus Swarm mode and an agent mode for monitoring multiple Docker hosts. The README says it does not store log files and does not support offline search.
use_cases: view live docker container logs in a browser
monitor container CPU and memory usage
watch logs from several containers side by side
monitor logs across multiple docker hosts
how_to_run: Or use Docker Compose with the amir20/dozzle:latest image, mounting /var/run/docker.sock and a dozzle_data volume, port 8080:8080
Swarm: docker service create with DOZZLE_MODE=swarm in global mode
Agent mode: docker run with the socket mounted, port 7007:7007, and the 'agent' argument
notable: Default image is built FROM scratch, about 7 MB compressed, with no shell
Works with Docker, Colima, and Podman via a remote socket
Agent mode lets one UI monitor several Docker hosts
Optional alpine image variants and version tags for pinning releases
caveats: No offline or historical log search; the README points to Loggly, Papertrail, or Kibana for that
Analytics via Google Analytics is on by default; disable with --no-analytics
